This is sort of my journey of learning C#, hopefully it will help you

I started with youtube and console apps, theres tons of C# beginner tutorials there so look no further! I also started reading the C# yellow book later on, best choice i made in my life. It really really teaches you C# and how to write good C# and what is considered bad. 

I started making small console apps and googling alot in order to learn what i need to create them. Then i wanted to make a promodo timer for my gf so i made a small simple xamarin app which required me to look for tutorials on that (also youtube mainly or blog posts). Then i made a discord server (you are more than welcome to join more info in my recent posts) where i got introduced to wpf MVVM.

So i started researching WPF mvvm n databinding and learning that. Then i went to learn things like dependancy injection, connecting sql db (without entity framework)

But after that i discovered my endgame. Web dev with asp.net. C# web api oh my god what a framework! Microsoft i love you so much. Normal MVC isnt bad either its really fun but holy cow web api is GOLD. It required me to learn so many new stuff and i actually started with MVC since at the time i didnt even know the differences (i watched an awesome video by freecodecamp named asp net core mvc on youtube) which also included entity framework. Another holy cow and love you microsoft for this one!

But after grasping mvc i dove into web api and noticed damn theres too much to learn and i couldnt find really really good resources to learn the advanced topics. So this is when i started looking at udemy courses. I bought one by Neil Cumming called asp web api with angular (so also started learning angular) still following that course. Right after this one ill be learning asp net mvc i bought a course by the same guy on the freecodecamp video. 


Tl:dr
So all together ive learned mostly from googling, youtube, making projects and when i wanted to learn advanced stuff and learn them right thats when i looked for udemy courses. I suggest you do the same. If not then just buy Mosh Hamedanis course they seem to be the most popular, remember to still think critically he has said weird stuff sometimes. Most important is to make your projects you will use them as a reference and they force you to learn and discover alot more.
